title: Orchestrate shimless language-client upgrade and staged API-surface deprecation playbook
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: safely upgrade transitive and direct dependencies across Python/JS/Go language clients and remove legacy API surface shims over a staged, observable rollout. Deliverables: (1) a per-language upgrade matrix with minimal breaking changes, (2) a compatibility shim removal schedule and runtime opt-in flags, (3) CI gates and e2e compatibility test suites, (4) migration docs and automated codemods for common breaking patterns, (5) rollback playbook and canary metrics. Success criteria: all three language clients publish patch/minor releases that pass the live-traffic smoke canaries, no critical regressions in the next 4 weeks, deprecation notice published and customer-facing migration guide available.
acceptance_criteria: All dependency bumps pass native unit and integration suites for Python/JS/Go
Compatibility shims behind feature flags and defaulted on for one release window
Automated codemod for the top-5 deprecated call sites per language published
Canary rollout to 5% of SDK traffic with latency and error-rate baselines monitored
Runbook and rollback steps documented and validated in staging
tasks: Audit current dependency versions and transitive tree for each client (dependabot + manual)
Produce language-specific upgrade matrix mapping breaking changes to API surface areas
Implement feature-flag toggle for compatibility shims in runtime and clients
Add CI job to run cross-language e2e against a pinned runtime (runtime-1.18) and latest models
Author codemods (jscodeshift, lib2to3-style, gofmt scripts) for common deprecated params
Write migration guide + Confluence page, link in release notes
Coordinate with SDK telemetry to add metrics for shim usage and rollback indicators
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Upgraded transitive dep introduces subtle behavior change (e.g. JSON parsing) — Mitigation: pin in-canary, add targeted unit tests + fuzzing for serialization paths
Risk: Customers using internal/undocumented API surface break when shims are removed — Mitigation: keep shims behind opt-out flag for two minor releases and proactively message affected customers
Risk: CI flakiness hides regressions across languages — Mitigation: add deterministic smoke tests and matrix on mac/linux/arm64 where relevant
Risk: Security vulnerabilities in new deps — Mitigation: security review before merge and upgrade only after CVE scanning passes
